# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the enrichment/categorization stage.

def run(bank, txns, accountType="SAVING", accountHolder="", do_purpose=True, do_clean=True):
    modname, fnname, extra = BANK_MAP[bank]
    mod = importlib.import_module("categorizationapp.BankScripts." + modname)
    fn = getattr(mod, fnname)
    rows = []
    for i, t in enumerate(txns):
        rows.append({
            "description": t.get("description", ""),
            "amount": t.get("amount", 100.0),
            "type": t.get("type", "DEBIT"),
            "balanceAfterTransaction": t.get("balanceAfterTransaction", 10000.0),
            "remark": t.get("remark", ""),
            "date": t.get("date", "2022-01-0%d" % ((i % 9) + 1)),
        })
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df = AppUtil.clean_input_df(df)
    if extra:
        df = fn(df, accountType, accountHolder)
    else:
        df = fn(df, accountType)
    if do_purpose:
        df = purpose(df, accountType)
    if do_clean:
        df = clean_names(df, accountType, bank)
    return df


def show(bank, descs, **kw):
    if isinstance(descs, str):
        descs = [{"description": descs}]
    descs = [({"description": d} if isinstance(d, str) else d) for d in descs]
    df = run(bank, descs, **kw)
    cols = [c for c in ["description", "type", "amount", "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory", "partyName", "merchantType"] if c in df.columns]
    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 60)
    print(df[cols].to_string())
    return df

    bank = sys.argv[1]
    desc = sys.argv[2]
    typ = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "DEBIT"
    amt = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 100.0
    show(bank, [{"description": desc, "type": typ, "amount": amt}])

        out.append({

            "description": t["description"],

            "partyName": r.get("partyName"),

        })
    return out

    res = snap("CANARA", CANARA) + snap("PNB", PNB)

todos.content: F-1: PNB bare-number cheque note (remark) debits mis-bucketed as TRANSFER
F-2: Canara CHQ PAID-MICR CLG- returns clearing tag instead of name
F-3: PNB generic NEFT credits get blank partyName (py_extract index)
F-4: PNB incoming IMPS P2A credits get reference number instead of sender name
F-5: Canara token verification credit filed as TRANSFER not ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION
Verify no baseline-correct rows moved (before/after diff)

steps.message:
All five findings traced to root cause and fixed. Every regression was localized to two bank scripts (`Canara.py`, `PNB.py` — the only two files in the tree with a modified mtime; every other module still carries the original 2022 timestamp).

## Root causes and fixes

| Finding | Bank | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-1 | PNB | `PNB.py:60` cheque-by-note rule for debits was `^[0-9]{5}$` while its credit twin on line 61 is `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. Every other bank in the repo uses an identical regex for the DEBIT/CREDIT pair, so 6-digit bare cheque notes on debits fell through to `TRANSFER`. | `^[0-9]{5}$` → `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| F-2 | Canara | `Canara.py:164` only recognised the `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-<name>` layout (name at dash-segment 2). `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` therefore fell to the generic `^CHQ PAID-` rule on line 165, which reads segment 1 — the clearing tag `MICR CLG`. | added the `Chq Paid-MICR CLG-` layout to line 164 |
| F-3 | PNB | `PNB.py:110` fallback NEFT name extraction used `py_extract(..., pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)`, but that pattern has a single capture group. `py_extract` returns `""` for a missing group, so the rule was dead code and every generic `NEFT ...` narration got a blank `partyName` (category stayed correct). It was the only `index=1` in the repo whose pattern has fewer than two groups. | `index=1` → `index=0` |
| F-4 | PNB | `PNB.py:94` matched only `^IMPSOUTP2A`; incoming IMPS P2A credits fell to the generic `^IMPS` rule on line 95, which reads slash-segment 3 (the account/reference number) instead of segment 2 (the sender name). The file pairs IN/OUT everywhere else (`^IMPSOUT|^IMPSIN`, `^NEFT OUT|^NEFT IN`, `^UPITROUT/|^UPITRIN`). | `^IMPSOUTP2A` → `^IMPSOUTP2A|^IMPSINP2A` |
| F-5 | Canara | `Canara.py:19` gated account-verification on `amount.lt(1)`, which can never be true for a ₹1 penny-drop, so token credits landed in `TRANSFER`. | `lt(1)` → `lt(2)` (matches HDFC/PNB; strictly a superset of the previous predicate, so no currently-matching row changes) |

## Verification

Built an offline harness (`/tmp/opencode/probe.py`, `corpus.py`) that replays a 92-row fixture set through the real enrichment path (bank script → `purpose` → `clean_names`) for both banks, covering ordinary purchases, UPI/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS in- and outbound layouts, cheques, cash, ECS/NACH, salary and verification credits.

- Before the change, all five findings reproduced exactly as described (e.g. `Micr Clg` as the counterparty, `'1234567890123'` as the sender name, ₹1 verification → `TRANSFER`).
- After the change, the before/after diff moves **only** rows of the five reported forms: the MICR-CLG cheques now yield the drawer's name, ₹1 verification credits yield `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, 6-digit-note cheque debits yield `CHEQUE_PAID`, incoming `IMPSINP2A` credits yield the sender's name, and generic `NEFT ` credits yield a name instead of blank. Every other row (ordinary UPI purchases, outbound IMPS, all other NEFT/RTGS layouts, generic `CHQ PAID-<name>`, `Home Clearing` cheques, card payments, cash deposits, auto-payments, salary) is byte-identical.
- Diff is 5 lines across 2 files; no shared regex constants or utility modules were touched, so no other bank can be affected. Also smoke-tested end-to-end through the Flask `/categorizeTransaction` endpoint.
